coordinates.object_orientation: +Z from beak/channel base to spire apex; aperture centre faces(+X,-Y) so mouth reads rightward in frontal -Y view. Dextral shell orientation, no mirroring. Base nearZ=0.

concept.reason: Scaled museum front/back photograph plus five real conspecific views expose form and damage boundaries; original description supports folds/cords. Sufficient for modest low-poly external study; no synthetic concept and no denied image action bypassed.

name: Hystrivasum vase-shell fossil
target: Original fossil-form target retained: stout vase-shaped shell, strong shoulder projections and open flaring mouth. Species-informed Hystrivasum squamosum, not generic conch or another Vasum genus.

reference_specimens.primary: UF201603, Neogene Atlas: Late Pliocene Tamiami Formation (Pinecrest Beds), Highlands County, Florida; two photographed views and2cm scale.
reference_specimens.comparison: H. Zell five-view H. squamosum photograph, original6000x4508px,2012. Shell has smaller bioerosion/edge damage but provides normal upper-whorl continuity and full side/top/bottom geometry; unnumbered and not used for scale.
reference_specimens.type_description: Hollister1971 description reproduced by Neogene Atlas; holotype PRI28201,122x90mm is a DIFFERENT specimen. Holotype image was not obtained.
reference_specimens.scope: Original low-poly genus-level fossil-shell study with modest evidence-based restoration of accidental damage, NOT exact UF specimen replica or scan. Upper UF holes are not natural shell openings.

must_have: Stout dextral biconic shell with relatively short broad spire and large body whorl; roughly5–6 externally visible whorl steps, not a Turritella tower
Strong shoulder row of outward-flared open scale-like projections, roughly10–14 simplified around the main shoulder; not evenly sharpened needle spines
Body whorl carries5 dominant spiral cords with broad low squamous flanges; smaller threads omitted
Body contracts into a waist above lower beak; lower beak has4–5 coarse spiral ridges and a broad open siphonal channel
Large ovate aperture on front-right with a flared, irregularly scalloped outer lip and real recessed cavity
Inner columellar lip bears3 transverse folds, strongest uppermost; rounded thick callus and perforate umbilical region beside canal
Upper sutural/shoulder collars remain rough and outward flared, not smooth steps or disconnected rings
must_not_have: No giant holes through upper whorls: UF front has major breakage; use the intact back and five-view comparison for continuous external surface
Do not replicate small worm borings, edge loss, catalogue handwriting, stains or exact photographic cracks
No speculative living mantle, tentacles, operculum, rock base or fossil association
No exaggerated straight blade/spike crown, trumpet-flat lip or long smooth straight siphonal tube
No false full internal chambers; only short visible cavity/columellar transition required
morphology.simplification: Prioritize stocky silhouette, shoulder scales,5 body cords, waist, aperture and3 columellar folds. Omit microscopic threads and most tiny scales; do not substitute a dense bump/noise texture for organized spiral structure.

scale.height_width_basis: UF image2cm scale strip spans approximately92px; shell height~490px and width~316px =>106.5x68.7mm. Approximate pixel/projection scale, not precise measurement.
scale.depth_basis: Inferred from conspecific five-view proportions; no direct UF thickness measurement.
scale.not_transferred: Type122x90mm is not UF201603; Zell specimen unknown dimensions are not assigned a scale or museum identity.

acceptance_focus: Front -Y: open ovate aperture,3 columellar folds and broad lower channel clearly readable
Side +X: projecting shoulder scales, constricted waist and flared lip have depth
Top +Z: dextral spiral structure and outward shoulder scale arrangement, no unrelated giant holes
Perspective(+X,-Y,+Z): stocky vase silhouette and organized ridges readable at card scale
No accidental floating scales, cracks between whorls or fake black decal cavity
evidence_limits: Accidental breakage is simplified/restored using intact areas and conspecific photo; not a restoration of exact missing fragments
Fine species delimitation can be variable; do not claim a diagnostic taxonomic revision or exact biological spine count
Neutral bone-beige is artistic fossil colour, not original living pattern
maker_workflow: 3–4 cheap gray checks before final rendering, specifically aperture, shoulder-scale silhouette and waist
Final front/side/top/perspective required; perspective may be preview. Extra only if specific unresolved feature demands it
Self-contained deterministic source; copy canonical helpers into source/deps and list relative paths/sha256, never import other model directories
Two isolated rebuilds, GLB/Khronos and required geometry checks remain; helper handoff is NOT scientific/visual PASS
Same localdir through maker and independent QA; maker sends root completion and FINAL, no upload/cleanup
